title: General-lfp integral inputs have complete constructible residue witnesses
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t$, and put $A=R/(t)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-étale site put $B=p_X^*\underline R$ and $A_X=p_X^*\underline A$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived category of module objects and relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_B)$ be bounded constructible in the general ring-object sense [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]: its bounded cohomology sheaves have finite constructible locally closed stratifications with locally finite presentations over $B$, allowing arbitrary local matrix entries.

Then $X$ is Noetherian, meaning quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. The ring $R$ is a discrete valuation ring and $A$ is a finite field of characteristic $\ell$. There is a canonical isomorphism of ring sheaves $B\cong\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(R/t^n)_X$, where the right-hand terms are constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The ring object $A_X$ is canonically the constant residue-field sheaf, with its ordinary relative derived tensor and finite constant local models.

Every cohomology sheaf of $M$ is constructible in the finite scalar local-model sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible], allowing finitely presented torsion $R$-modules. The object $M$ is locally derived $(t)$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]. There is a bounded étale $A$-complex $C_M$ with constructible finite-dimensional cohomology [def-pe-etale-constructible-module], of finite Tor amplitude, and an isomorphism
$$\nu_X^*C_M\simeq M\otimes_B^L A_X,$$
where $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ is the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Finite Tor amplitude means that there are integers $a\le b$ such that $H^q(C_M\otimes_A^L N)=0$ for every degree-zero étale $A$-module sheaf $N$ and $q\notin[a,b]$. No completeness or scalar-model assumption is imposed on $M$.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1, Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); agent extraction for a general ring-object input via lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison. Coefficient preparation uses the existing DVR, coefficient-limit and finite-discrete comparison nodes.

proof.text: The only ideals of the field $k$ are $0$ and $k$, so $k$ is Noetherian. The single affine chart of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ therefore makes it locally Noetherian, and the affine quasi-compactness theorem makes it quasi-compact. Apply the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: $X$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. The locally-Noetherian quasi-separatedness theorem now gives quasi-separatedness of $X$. In particular $X$ is qcqs. A locally Noetherian affine covering of $X$ has a finite subcover by quasi-compactness, so $X$ also satisfies the finite-affine-cover formulation of Noetherian used by the adic criterion.

Apply the integers-of-a-finite-extension theorem to $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. It gives that $R$ is a DVR with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_E$, and $R/\mathfrak m_E$ is a finite field. By the definition of uniformizer, $(t)=\mathfrak m_E$, so this residue field is precisely $A=R/(t)$. The extended absolute value restricts to the $\ell$-adic one, hence $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$. Thus $\ell\in\mathfrak m_E$ and $\ell=0$ in $A$. Since $A$ is a nonzero field and $\ell$ is prime, its characteristic is $\ell$. This argument allows arbitrary ramification and $\ell=2$.

source.place: Section 6.8, finite-extension coefficient convention; arithmetic supplied by the existing finite-extension integers theorem and the definition of uniformizer.

proof.text: Use clause (3) of the integral coefficient-limit theorem, with $t$ as uniformizer, to identify $B=p_X^*\underline R$ canonically with $\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(R/t^n)_X$ as a ring sheaf, with the indicated quotient transition maps. Apply the finite-discrete coefficient equivalence to the finite commutative field $A$ from step 2: $p_X^*\underline A$ is the constant ring sheaf $A_X$. Its exact derived equivalence preserves the relative derived tensor, every Tor interval and the finite constant local models. These are the coefficient identifications required in the statement.

source.place: Section 6.5, coefficient convention preceding Definition 6.5.1; Lemma 4.2.12 for continuous coefficient sheaves, and the finite-discrete coefficient comparison.

proof.text: Choose a bounded cohomological interval for $M$. For each of its cohomology sheaves $H^q(M)$, the hypothesis is condition (i) of the integral lfp/constant-model comparison: finite constructible locally closed strata and local finite presentations with arbitrary sections as matrix entries. Step 1 verifies its Noetherian hypothesis. Apply implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii), with its scalar ring denoted $R$ here. It gives finite constant scalar local models $B_V\otimes_R P$ for finitely presented $R$-modules $P$. The theorem explicitly allows torsion $P$ and does not assume completeness. Consequently every $H^q(M)$ is constructible in the scalar-model sense, and $M$ is still bounded in its original interval; no change to the complex is made.

source.place: The existing coefficient-specific lfp/constant-model comparison, with its continuous-matrix descent argument; compare Theorem 6.2(2),(3) and Theorem 6.12(2). Bhatt–Scholze Definition 6.8.10 fixes the resulting scalar-model notion.

proof.text: Apply the integral cohomological adic criterion, implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(2), with its $(R,\pi,k,K)$ equal to our $(R,t,A,M)$. Step 1 supplies its Noetherian scheme, step 3 its completed coefficient sheaf and residue quotient, and step 4 its bounded scalar-model constructible cohomology. If module objects are used, take their section-ring presentation through the module-object/ringed-site comparison: its equivalence leaves underlying abelian sheaves unchanged and identifies the ordinary unbounded derived relative tensors, also on slices. Thus the criterion applies to exactly the given object and tensor. It yields local derived $(t)$-completeness in the stated sense, and a bounded étale complex $C_M$ with constructible finite-dimensional $A$-cohomology and an isomorphism $\nu_X^*C_M\simeq M\otimes_B^L A_X$. Its Tor conclusion is explicitly quantified over all degree-zero étale $A$-module sheaves $N$, with one ordered interval $[a,b]$. The finite-discrete equivalence of step 3 and the section-ring comparison identify these conclusions with the module-object formulations in the item; they introduce no completion assumption on $M$.
